title: Cylinder criterion for a full quotient functor to be a localization
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories in fixed containing universes, $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a full and essentially surjective functor, and $V$ any class of morphisms of $\mathcal C$. Here fullness means surjectivity on every morphism set, and essential surjectivity means that every object of $\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to some $L(X)$. Assume that $L(v)$ is an isomorphism for every $v\in V$. Assume also that whenever $f_0,f_1:X\to Y$ satisfy $L(f_0)=L(f_1)$, there are an object $I$, morphisms $i_0,i_1:X\to I$, $\pi:I\to X$ and $H:I\to Y$, with $\pi i_0=\pi i_1=1_X$, $Hi_0=f_0$, $Hi_1=f_1$, and $\pi\in V$. Then $L$ is a localization of $\mathcal C$ at $V$, with the functor and natural-transformation universal property of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. No model structure, additive structure or closure condition on $V$ is required.
